key_insight: FinTradeBench introduces a benchmark that evaluates LLMs on realistic financial decision-making by combining heterogeneous signals (regulatory fundamentals + price-derived trading signals), revealing gaps in current LLM financial reasoning beyond static balance-sheet QA.
problem_solved: Existing financial QA benchmarks focus narrowly on balance-sheet or textual facts; FinTradeBench addresses the need to test LLMs on integrated, multi-signal financial reasoning tasks that mirror real-world investment and trading decisions.
method: Assemble a curated dataset linking company filings (fundamentals) with time-series market data to compute trading signals and construct multi-signal inputs.
Design a suite of financial reasoning tasks (e.g., valuation judgement, short-to-medium term trading recommendation, signal interpretation) and standardized evaluation protocols.
Evaluate common LLMs with baseline prompting/fine-tuning strategies, report quantitative performance gaps, and analyze error modes tied to signal integration and temporal reasoning.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a focused benchmark to measure and improve LLM capabilities on realistic finance problems, guiding model selection, fine-tuning, and architecture choices for trading and investment applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: filings + price time series -> signal computation -> LLM -> decision/recommendation
Example task card: input (excerpt of filing + indicator chart) and desired reasoning steps + gold answer
Bar chart comparing LLM performance across tasks (valuation, trading, interpretation) to highlight weaknesses
Error-mode matrix: types of mistakes (temporal misalignment, misinterpreting fundamentals, over-reliance on one signal)
paper_title: FinTradeBench: A Financial Reasoning Benchmark for LLMs
paper_authors: Yogesh Agrawal, Aniruddha Dutta, Md Mahadi Hasan, Santu Karmaker, Aritra Dutta
